method: Rows = docs/parity/inventory-net.json items in inventory order (395), ids copied verbatim; the id order is asserted by the generator. Code refs are resolved mechanically: each row names (file, regex) pairs and the generator writes the path:line of the first (or n-th) matching line, failing when a pattern does not match; tests are resolved by exact test-function name (optionally 'file::name') against an ast walk of tests/**/test_*.py (every def test_* with its file) and the generator fails on a missing or ambiguous name, so every cited test exists. Enumeration of our side per inventory kind: (1) net:cfg:<op> - builder grep in custom_components/junghome_ble/jhmesh/config_messages.py (^def <name>) and its senders: grep -rnw <builder> custom_components tools (commission.py plan phases, mesh_config.py _step/_bind_step/remove_node, audit.py _SETTING_GETS/_model_gets, coordinator.py heartbeats, tools/cli_ops.py config_*), plus the key-refresh follower in jhmesh/client.py (CONFIG_NETKEY_UPDATE / CONFIG_KEY_REFRESH_PHASE_SET); status rule for app-unused messages: implemented when a flow of ours sends it with a test (we exceed the app), else na citing the inventory's 'no class outside no/nordicsemi references it'. (2) net:proxycfg - jhmesh/pdu.py proxy_config_* and jhmesh/client.py set_filter/_resend_filter. (3) net:addr / net:alloc / net:range - DEVICE_TYPE_GROUPS, TIME_KEEPER_GROUP, ALL_SCENES/ALL_NODES, ProjectFile.add_group/free_group_address/add_scene/free_scene_number, commission._allocate, vault.choose_ranges, onboarding.free_unicast_block, and the central entities in light.py/cover.py/switch.py/climate.py (grep 0xFEF5..0xFEF9). (4) net:uc / net:svc / net:ui - mapped to the HA actions in services.yaml (27 actions: set_room create_room rename_room delete_room assign_key clear_key create_scene rename_scene store_scene remove_from_scene delete_scene sync_gateway get_schedules create_schedule enable_schedule disable_schedule delete_schedule set_threshold delete_threshold audit_network export_network find_new_devices add_device remove_device start_dim stop_dim step_dim) and their implementations (services.py _<action>, mesh_config.MeshConfigurator methods, schedules.Scheduler, thresholds.py, onboard.py, keep_awake.py), the coordinator's connect sequence (_after_connect, _send_time, _send_location, _refresh_all/_chunked, async_follow_gateway), entities (config_entities.py target builders, switch.JungHomeWalkingTest, climate/cover/light/switch central entities, scene.py), the config flow (upload / gateway / reconfigure steps) and identity.py/jhmesh/vault.py; an app step with no counterpart in that list is a gap or a partial 'missing'. (5) net:debug - each hidden-screen action mapped to a tools/mesh_poc.py sub-command (build_parser: set/get to groups, prop get/set/list/lists, config get-composition/audit/hops/hopmatrix/publication/subscribe/unsubscribe/subscriptions/bind/unbind, sched, scene-actions, health, provision), the audit_network / export_network actions, diagnostics.py, or the repairs (skip ahead); a read/write with no builder or sender (grep ^def <builder> in jhmesh/messages.py, opcode-only constants) is a gap. (6) net:export / net:db - jhmesh/export.py META_KEYS and every writer of a meta key (grep -rn '<metaKey>' custom_components tools); a key only carried through verbatim (round trip) is partial or gap depending on whether its feature exists. (7) net:http - gateway_api.JungHomeGatewayApi methods (version GET version/, register POST register, register_by_password, fetch_project GET project/junghome|project/cdb, upload_project POST config project_file); any other body/path is a gap. (8) net:pref / net:enum - the equivalent state or codec (CONF_GATEWAY_SYNCED digest, ISSUE_GATEWAY_SYNC repair, properties.py codecs KEY_MODE/BUTTON_LAYOUT/EDGE_BEHAVIOUR/ASTRO_MODE/PropertyModeCodec/SceneConfigCodec, vendor_models SCHEDULE_TYPES/ACTION_*/DAYS, export GROUP_FUNCTIONS/FUNCTION_KEY_MODE/KEY_MODE_SERVERS, mesh_config KEY_MODE_CLIENTS/ROOM_FUNCTIONS). Status rules: implemented = code + a test that exercises the behaviour and the inventory details matched (encodings, values, sequence) or deliberately exceeded; partial = code exists but a behaviour in the details is missing or differs (the 'missing' text says which), or code without a behaviour test; gap = no implementing code for the behaviour (a row may still cite a builder or codec it would use); na = only with a concrete reason: the app never sends it (unused Nordic classes), JUNG cloud participation (docs/gap-analysis/network-features.md sec. 8.2 'HA should not become a cloud participant', replaced by review-3 N1 provisioner identity and W1 re-apply), local-only phone UI state that is not in the project file, the IV-index debug hacks (review-3 N13), or behaviour that would harm Home Assistant's own link (proxy filter address lists). feasibility (partial/gap) is one of: offline with tests/sim + unit tests; offline against a faked gateway REST API; needs a capture of the app on the installation; needs a device class the installation lacks; destructive (spare device); needs firmware-update support (review-3 N9); needs a spare app install to import an HA-written file (review-3 N1). Line numbers are 1-based at the time of writing; rerun = regenerate with the same (file, regex) and test-name lists. Verification pass (adversarial, against the jadx source and the code): every gap / partial / na row was re-searched in custom_components and tools (grep -rn over builder names, opcodes, property ids, REST paths and service names) and re-read in the jadx source; implemented rows spot-checked for encoding/sequence and for the cited test asserting it: net:uc:createelementconnectiongroups, net:uc:connecttoaddress, net:uc:setsceneconnection (additive-first order is the deliberate mesh_config.ordered rule), net:alloc:element-group, net:cfg:803d, net:uc:createthreshold, net:cfg:03, net:uc:addgrouptodevices, net:uc:configurepublicationforsensorserver, net:alloc:room-group, net:addr:0xffff, net:uc:keeplowpowerdeviceawake, net:uc:resetkeysetpropertymode (sent after the Config plan by design), net:uc:loadinitialdevicestate, net:uc:connecttodevicetypegroup, net:uc:exportprojecttogateway, net:uc:togglejhschedule, net:debug:sensorsettingsviewmodel.requestsensordescriptor, net:debug:projectdebugviewmodel.exportproject / importproject. Rows changed by it carry the corrected status; four rows were added for the inventory's click-handler items (inventory method step 13). matches the app: an automatic upload that fails is tried again twice, 15 s apart (GATEWAY_UPLOAD_RETRIES / GATEWAY_UPLOAD_RETRY_DELAY = the app's flow retry(2) with a 15000 ms delay), with the same export, and the time of a successful upload is kept (CONF_GATEWAY_LAST_SYNC). Deliberate differences: only failures a retry can fix are retried (gateway unreachable / busy / HTTP error, or its export could not be fetched for the pre-upload check); a refusal of ours (the gateway holds changes HA has not seen, a pin it contradicts, a rejected token) is final, since retrying cannot change it and the repairs say what to do; the next change's upload or sync_gateway supersedes a pending retry (the app's newer upload does the same by uploading the newer export); sync_gateway itself is not retried in the background, the user who called it gets the error. The pending retry is the entry's (hass.data by entry id, a Home Assistant background task), not the configurator's: most changes reload the entry right after they are saved, so each attempt waits out a reload in progress and goes through the configurator of the moment with the export on disk (every later save cancels the retry first, so that is the failed change's export); an entry not loaded after all ends it, removing the entry cancels it. A gateway that stops answering (the app's 404 = any transport failure, or another certificate) is looked for over the mesh by re-reading 0xC002 / 0xC003 (async_follow_gateway), once per outage rather than every 10 s; the token 0xC001 is the app's and deliberately never taken, so a 401 raises the gateway_token_rejected repair instead, and while that repair is open the polls do not ask (no rejected token every 30 s / 5 min, the warning logged once); the reconfigure that clears it, or an export fetch that is answered, resumes them. The gateway is only asked once its node vouched for the pin (gateway_vouched).

Per room: the same four classes for each room that has such loads (Devices.room_members, the app's DeviceFilter.Group), named 'All <kind> in <room>'. As the app's area sheet: on / off, positions, slats and set-points are one Unacknowledged Set per member (CommunicateWithDevice, no status awaited), a dim level and a blind stop one message to the room address. The room entities sit on the mesh device, not in the room's area, so an area-targeted action does not reach the loads twice. A room deleted, or left without loads of a kind, takes its central entity out of the entity registry at the next setup (the mesh device stays, so device pruning never reaches them).
